### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.api__ListInstalledPackagesRequest__limit.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.api__ListInstalledPackagesRequest__limit.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1f69917c5c76c065256a9bbaac3afc587279b9ba` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3c80a927fe155e992de77228462a849d6ef8ca6f` — the merge of head `a755473aac4018b3974315940594b704bf139c7d` into base `1f69917c5c76c065256a9bbaac3afc587279b9ba`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 3c80a927fe155e992de77228462a849d6ef8ca6f && git checkout 3c80a927fe155e992de77228462a849d6ef8ca6f

git fetch origin 1f69917c5c76c065256a9bbaac3afc587279b9ba a755473aac4018b3974315940594b704bf139c7d && git checkout -B drift-repro 1f69917c5c76c065256a9bbaac3afc587279b9ba && git merge --no-ff a755473aac4018b3974315940594b704bf139c7d
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a755473aac4018b3974315940594b704bf139c7d`

### ① Derived judgments

**The enumeration work is right.** Everything below was measured in my own detached worktree at the head, nothing adopted from the report or the card.

**1. The serving door, read first-hand.** `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, the `parts.length === 0 && m === 'GET'` branch opening at `:809`. Every `query` occurrence from `:809` to that branch's `return` is one of five, covering exactly three keys: `enabled` — `readEnabledFilter(query?.enabled)` at `:828`, applied at `:845` as `packageCountsAsEnabled(p) === enabled.value`; `status` at `:837`/`:838`; `type` at `:840`/`:841`. No fourth key. The only other `limit`/`cursor` token in the whole file is the `hasMore` comment at `:874`. The card's premise holds and the report's line numbers reproduce exactly.

**2. Incomplete, not falsified — and the diff honours that.** I reassembled the concatenated `PACKAGES_LIST_PAGINATION_REMOVED` literal at base `1f69917c5c` and at the head: 986 → 1009 characters. Applying exactly two substitutions to the base string reproduces the head string **byte-for-byte** — so the claim of minimality is not the author's word, it is reproducible. The load-bearing claim *「no page was ever withheld and no continuation token was ever minted」* is present, in place and byte-identical; so are the `.default(50)` passage, the `hasMore` passage and the closing cursor-design sentence. The argument survives because it is still true at the door: `enabled` selects rows, it mints nothing and withholds no page. No exclusion was added; the sentence still enumerates.

**3. Carrier sweep, run independently** — five spellings over every tracked file, not the report's table. Carriers of the old two-filter enumeration remaining anywhere in the tree: **two, both under `.changeset/`** (flagged in ③). **Zero** under `packages/` or `content/`. I specifically went looking for the **#19523 shape** and it does not apply here: the sibling retired-key entry `18.api__ListInstalledPackagesRequest__cursor.ts` **exists** and deliberately does not repeat the enumeration — it defers to the `limit` entry (「see the sibling entry … for the full record」), so there is no second entry silently left behind. `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` and `packages/spec/spec-changes.json` genuinely do not carry the sentence: the guide renders 16 → 17 and step 18 is not rendered yet, which is why `check:upgrade-guide` is green rather than blind.

**4. The generated mirrors are the tooling's.** At the head I ran `gen:migration-registry`, then `gen:schema` and `gen:docs`. `git status --porcelain` was empty after each. `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` and `content/docs/references/api/package-api.mdx` are byte-identical to what this repo's own generators produce — no hand edit anywhere. `packages/spec/json-schema/` is untracked build output and picks the repaired string up on regeneration.

**5. The published docs page is true, not merely consistent with the tombstone.** `content/docs/references/api/package-api.mdx:405-406` (`+2/−2`) now tells a reader the door filters on `status` / `type` / `enabled` and to filter with all three. Checked against the door rather than against the source string: all three are declared `.optional()` on `ListInstalledPackagesRequestSchema` and all three are read. The page already advertised `enabled | boolean | optional | Filter by enabled state`, and since #19405 that advertisement is true — this change makes the tombstone row stop contradicting the row four lines above it. The page carries the AUTO-GENERATED banner and regenerates clean.

**6. The in-place docblock repair is justified and keeps its guardrail.** The old paragraph asserted `enabled` 「is still declared here and still unread by that door … PENDING」 — that is **falsified outright** by `:828`, not merely incomplete, so freezing it was not an option the way freezing an enumeration might have been. It discharges on the condition it names, it is forty lines from the tombstone in the same file, and it is inside the claim's declared surface. The replacement keeps the ⛔ against closing the divergence by deleting `enabled` and adds the reason («the door reads it»). Shipping the tombstone without it would have landed a file that says the door filters on `enabled` and, forty lines down, that the door does not read it. Accepted as declared.

**7. What I tried that did not break it.** A PASS-shaped list, offered here because the failure in ② is not about this work:
- Parsed the schema at the head: `{}`, `{status, enabled, type}` and `{enabled: false}` accept; `{limit: 1}`, `{cursor: 'x'}` and `{status: 'running'}` refuse on their own issue paths; `{unknownKey: 1}` still parses clean and strips (the schema is not `.strict()`, which is the whole reason for `retiredKey()`). The `z.object({ … })` literal is untouched by the diff, so the accept/refuse set is identical to the base — only the refusal *text* moved.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` → exit 0, 508 files passed / 1 skipped, 14893 passed / 1 skipped / 1 todo. (The report reads 509 / 14895 / 1 todo; the one skipped file here is environmental, not a finding.)
- Hunted for a consumer that parses the enumeration. There is none. The pin at `packages/spec/src/api/package-api.test.ts` anchors the prefix, the `17.5.0 (ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove)` clause, `` `.default(50)` `` and `Delete the key.` — never the filter list. So no test could have caught this defect and none breaks now; I agree no new pin belongs here, since a mechanical one would have to reach across into the runtime.
- Checked the semantic entry's **untouched** `acceptanceCriteria` for collateral falsification by #19405, since that is where a careless repair would have left damage: it says a request still carrying `?limit=1&cursor=x` is IGNORED, not refused, and that an unknown key has never produced a 400. Still true — `readEnabledFilter` can answer 400, but only on the *declared* `enabled` key; `limit` and `cursor` remain unread. Correctly left alone.

### ② Semver level

**Prose-only, plainly.** No key is added or removed, no type changes, no accept set moves in either direction. `limit` and `cursor` stay `retiredKey()` tombstones typed `never`; `status` / `type` / `enabled` were all already declared. The only published thing that moves is the *text* of a refusal message plus two generated mirrors of it. So `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` is the **right level**, and `skip-changeset` would be wrong — the string ships in `dist`.

**But `Clause-②: yes` is wrong, and it is red on this head right now.** Clause ② is the declaration 「this PR puts a new key on a published payload」; this PR puts none. `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s level axis refuses `yes` + `patch`, and the `Check Changeset` job on `a755473aac` (job `106359329145`) exited **1** on exactly that:

```
⛔ This PR declares clause-② `yes`, and it grades NO package whose `packages/**/src/**` it moves
   at `minor` or above.
     - @objectstack/spec: patch
```

Reproduced offline in my worktree at the head, base `1f69917c5c`, with the PR's own body and labels as the event payload: **exit 1**. The same command with no `pull_request` payload: **exit 0**, printing `LEVEL AXIS: NOT APPLICABLE — this run has no pull_request to read a declaration from`. That is the mechanism of the miss: a local derived-gate sweep cannot reach this axis, so a report reconciling 104 families locally reads green while the PR's own required-lane job is red.

**Remedy, and it is route 2 of the two the gate names, not route 1.** Correct the declaration to `Clause-②: no` at its producer — claim `5760763611` and the PR body. ⛔ Do **not** clear the red by raising `@objectstack/spec` to `minor`: that publishes a false widening signal into a lockstep fixed group for a diff that changes a comment and a string, which is the gate's own route 1 applied to a PR that never widened anything. ⛔ The `needs:contract-review` carrier is not part of this remedy either.

### ③ Boundary flags

**1. Two unrepaired carriers — reported correctly, not widened into correctly, but not filed.** `.changeset/17667-packages-query-contract.md:14` and `.changeset/scoped-packages-dispatcher-door.md:13` still carry the two-filter enumeration and publish into the same 17.5.0 release. Both are outside the claim's declared file surface and reporting rather than widening is the right call. The deadline the PR names is real and written down: a released `CHANGELOG.md` entry is amendable only by a dedicated docs-only PR against that entry. **#19523 exists because a near-identical sentence shipped in two carriers and only one was repaired** — the same shape is live here in the open direction, and it is recorded only in a PR body and an `out_of_scope_findings` string with no card behind it. File one before the 17.5.0 cut. One mitigation the PR does not claim, and it is worth having on the record: both affected packages' 17.5.0 changelogs will carry a correction in the same document — the spec's from this PR's own changeset, which quotes FROM → TO, and the runtime's from `.changeset/19394-packages-list-door-enabled-filter.md`. That softens the hazard; it does not close it.

**2. The dual carrier is hung on one side.** `needs:contract-review` is on card #19407 and not on PR #19595 (labels read: `documentation`, `size/s`, `tooling`). Flagged as a reading only — this review moves no label.

**3. Two files sit outside the claim's declared surface, and rightly.** `content/docs/references/api/package-api.mdx` and the new `.changeset/` entry are both outside `packages/spec/src/{migrations,api}/`. The first is generated and gate-forced, the second is mandatory for anything that publishes. The distinction the PR draws — tooling-owned mirrors move with the source, hand-written files outside the fence do not — is the right line and is the reason flag 1 above is a flag rather than a finding.

**4. `ListInstalledPackagesResponseSchema.nextCursor` stays declared and never emitted.** Agreed as an observation, not a half-done card: it is declared-and-unemitted on the *response* side, which widens no accept set, and the `hasMore` comment argues the position. Correctly left alone.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-19407-list-door-tombstone-enumerates-two-of-three`
Reviewed-by: `session_01AmH9bKvGoLjiY86Q4Z3og2`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a755473aac4018b3974315940594b704bf139c7d`

### ① Derived judgments

**This record supersedes `5762666543` on the same head.** No new commit — the remedy was the PR-body edit `pr-automation.yml` subscribes `edited` for. What I checked to say so: the three commits are unchanged and the newest (`a755473aac40`) was committed `13:25:28Z`, *before* round 1's `15:03:08Z` record; no `head_ref_force_pushed` event on the timeline; 6 files, `+56/−18`; merge base `1f69917c5c` in round 1's job and in every run since. The diff is byte-identical to what round 1 reviewed, so round 1's confirmations are adopted rather than re-litigated — nothing in my own reading contradicts them.

**1. The declaration is now right.** The body carries `Clause-②: no`, bare, at the start of line 3, exactly once. Judged from the diff and the card, ⛔ not from the path surface: clause ② is the assertion 「this PR puts a new key on a published payload」, and this diff puts none. The only hunks in `packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts` are at `:199` and `:207` (the two `PACKAGES_LIST_PAGINATION_REMOVED` substitutions) and `:221` (the docblock forty lines down) — **no hunk reaches the `z.object({ … })` literal**, so no key is added, removed or retyped. The other five files are a retired-key record comment, the semantic entry's `replacement` / `reason`, the generated registry, the generated `.mdx`, and the new changeset. `no` is the true answer.

**2. The footer round-trip cost nothing.** The stored body carries exactly one `---` rule and exactly one `_Generated by [Claude Code]…_` footer, one `Fixes #19407`, one `Clause-②:` line and one `Authored in …` line. All eight `##` sections are present, in round 1's order, and the body terminates cleanly. No prose was lost. On the process conflict the dev disclosed: outside my scope, and it left no mark on the artifact — which is the only part that could have been a finding.

### ② Semver level

**`patch` is correct and ⛔ route 1 was not taken.** `.changeset/19407-packages-list-tombstone-third-filter.md` still grades `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, and it is the only changeset this PR adds. The level did not move. Prose-only is the right reading: no key, no type, no accept-set change — only a refusal string and two generated mirrors of it.

**⚠️ But `Check Changeset` is red on this head right now, and it is no longer the body's fault.** Four runs, all on `a755473aac`, all against merge base `1f69917c5c`:

| run | created | `Clause-②:` line read | carrier read | Check Changeset |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `35607874745` | 13:47:27Z | `yes` | not on this PR (3 labels) | ❌ failure — round 1's job `106359329145` |
| `35621948851` | 15:53:05Z | `no` | not on this PR (3 labels) | ✅ **success** |
| `35622049512` | 15:54:00Z | `no` | not on this PR (3 labels) | ✅ **success** |
| `35622507496` | 15:58:08Z | `no` | **`needs:contract-review` IS on this PR** | ❌ failure — job `106408757990` |

⇒ **Round 1's FAIL ground is discharged, and the gate itself is what proves it.** The two middle runs print `✓ LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② 'no', so no package here is declared to have grown a published surface`. The body edit alone turned the axis green, twice, on this head, with nothing pushed — exactly the `edited`-trigger path. Manufacturing a `synchronize` commit would indeed have been the workaround that trigger exists to avoid.

**What re-reddened it is a second producer of the same declaration, and it is not the dev's.** `needs:contract-review` was applied to this PR at `15:58:06Z` (timeline `labeled` event; it had been hung only on card #19407 — round 1's own flag 2). `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads clause ② from the label **or** the line:

```js
if (carrier || (line?.kind === 'declared' && line.value === 'yes')) return { value: 'yes', … };
```

and it reads labels from the frozen event payload. So the `labeled` run saw `Clause-②: no` **and** the carrier, resolved `yes`, and refused `yes` + `patch` again. The file says so in its own words: 「a carrier alone forces `yes` … and only the review seat can clear it」.

**This is the designed order, not a defect, and ⛔ no commit can clear it.** Same file: 「THE CARRIER IS STRIPPED AT REVIEW PASS, so a run after the PASS no longer reads a `yes` from it. That is the intended order — the human review that clears the carrier is the authority on the level.」 The carrier is what holds this PR outside the merge queue until this review lands, so failing the PR for its presence would make it unstrippable. `pull_request` is subscribed to `unlabeled`, so stripping it fires a run that reads no carrier — and the two greens above are the measurement that the axis then passes. ⛔ Route 1 (raising `@objectstack/spec` to `minor`) stays wrong for the reason round 1 gave: a false widening signal into a lockstep fixed group for a diff that moves a comment and a string.

I move no label, so the lane is red as I write. **Clearing it is the seat's single remaining act: strip `needs:contract-review` from PR #19595.**

### ③ Boundary flags

**1. The carrier red above.** The only thing between this PR and a green required lane, and it is the seat's to clear, not the dev's. Named here so a PASS is not misread as "all green".

**2. The dual carrier is now hung on the other side.** Round 1 read `needs:contract-review` on card #19407 and not on the PR; it is now on both. That closed round 1's flag 2 and opened flag 1 above. A reading only — this review moves no label.

**3. Two unrepaired `.changeset/` carriers, still unfiled.** `.changeset/17667-packages-query-contract.md:14` and `.changeset/scoped-packages-dispatcher-door.md:13`. The head has not moved, so they stand exactly as round 1 left them, deadline included: file a card before the 17.5.0 cut. Correctly reported rather than widened into.

**4. `ListInstalledPackagesResponseSchema.nextCursor` stays declared and never emitted.** Unchanged, and agreed as an observation rather than a half-done card.

## ⛔ Seat correction — comment `5763350805` breached the dev's standing contract, and the contract stands, 2026-09-21T16:13Z

The dev flagged the body edit it was asked for as **non-precedent** and was right to. Recording the
resolution so the next reader does not take it as one.

**The line, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md:56`, read first-hand:**

> PR 正文 dev 只写一次,在开 PR 那一笔,⛔ 不 `PATCH`;事后要改的报告点名改法,席位代写。

⇒ the dev writes the PR body **once**, at PR-open, and ⛔ never `PATCH`es it. A later change is **named
in the report** and the **seat** writes it. My handback assigned that write back to the dev, which is
exactly the act the line forbids.

**Resolution: the line stands unchanged, and the error is this seat's.** ⛔ Not a contract conflict and
⛔ not a case for amending the file — the rule was clear, this seat read it wrong. The
`Clause-②: yes`→`no` edit on this PR was a **seat** write in every sense that matters: the declaration
is the seat's own, dictated in the claim comment, and the correction record for it
(`Clause-②-correction: 5760763611`) is a seat artefact. It should have gone out as a seat `PATCH`, not
as a dispatch line.

⚠️ **One thing the episode did surface, and it is filed rather than settled here.** A body `PATCH` and a
body `POST` do not store the same bytes: a create with a tail session-URL footer stores one footer, and
a `PATCH` carrying the same tail makes the platform append a **second** bare one. That is a real cost
attached to the seat's half of this rule, it argues for nothing about who writes, and it is written up
with its repair shape on card #19606 — ⛔ not here.

⛔ Nothing above changes this PR, its review record, or its verdict.
